layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must revert them. The effect iterator

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models such an activation (Section 3.1.3), each of its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: iterations yielding the modified context, an inverse, and a continuation, and a component's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whole activation is one run of

layout_dets.text: , following

layout_dets.text: Definition 18, so that the accumulator applies the inverses in last-in-first-out order.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Deactivation. A deactivation enters from either stage of the lifecycle: L-Divert takes out a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fiber whose transition is still in progress, and L-Leave one that is Active. It cannot be taken in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: one step. A component being torn down because its provider is going away is running its own

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teardown code, which may need the very coeffect that is being withdrawn; closing a connection

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pool typically means handing the connections back to whatever provided them. The consumer

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: must therefore still be able to read the key throughout its own deactivation, and the provider's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: withdrawal must take effect only afterwards, which gives content to the ordering Section 3.2

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: requires of dependencies and dependents. A deactivation taken in one step would remove

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the provisions and run the inverse together, with no interval between them for a consumer's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: teardown to occupy. The rules below therefore separate the decision from the act, and the act

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is guarded by the following condition.

layout_dets.text: L-Divert may fall between any two consecutive iterations of a transition, routing the fiber

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: into Unloading with the inverses accumulated so far rather than applying them on the spot.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Routing through Active instead would let the fiber provide its coeffects for the length of one

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: step and oblige its dependents to activate against a component that is already leaving. The first

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of L-Divert's two alternatives aborts the iteration the fiber is holding, which only an iteration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundary makes possible, so the granularity at which a divert may fall is that of the iterator;

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the second lets that iteration land, serving the host Section 4.4 admits, in which an iteration in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: flight cannot be declined.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: L-Leave records the decision to deactivate without acting on it, which stops the fiber

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: providing its coeffects while leaving its own committed view and everyone else's intact. L-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Unload applies the accumulator, discards the committed view, and leaves the fiber Inactive; it is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the only rule in the calculus that applies an accumulator, an L-Divert routing here rather than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: applying one of its own.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The two requirements are then carried by different parts of the form: the consumer's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reading by the committed view, which L-Unload discards as its last act, and the deferral of the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: withdrawal by the premise

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , which we call the guard and which holds a provider's

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: withdrawal back until every consumer that resolves a key to n has gone. For a fiber L-Divert

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: takes out of its first transition the guard is vacuous, a fiber that has never been Active providing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nothing and appearing in no committed view. Theorem 70 establishes both requirements.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The guard is imposed per binding rather than per fiber:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tests whether some

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: committed view names

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: so a fiber that declares none of n's keys is no obstacle, and neither

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is one that resolved a key of n's in another realm (Section 3.2.3). Under the single-source

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: discipline of O-Insert the per-binding reading coincides with the coarser test

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , a key having one possible provider there.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A guard of this kind ordinarily deadlocks. What keeps it from doing so is Unloading together

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: being the union over Active fibers alone: once L-Leave or L-Divert has marked

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: table leaves

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: so no target view can name n any longer, and every consumer that committed

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to n is itself on its way out. Theorem 73 turns that into the claim that the guard always releases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The guard orders deactivations along coeffects and not along the fiber tree: a parent may

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: run its inverse while a child of it is still Unloading, since relied speaks only of committed views.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parent and child are accordingly ordered more weakly than Theorem 70 orders a provider and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: its consumer, and a parent and a child whose effects meet at a shared key are governed by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pairwise independence of Lemma 66 instead.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The rules are nondeterministic: several fibers may hold a committed view differing from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: their target view, and the relation commits to no order among them. They are also reactive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: only, in that no rule mentions a scheduler; the steps are any sequence of rule applications, so

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a theorem proved over all such sequences holds for every scheduling policy a runtime might

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adopt.
